::: {#def-bootstrap-ci-bca}
#### Bias-corrected and accelerated bootstrap confidence interval

With the [bias correction](#def-bca-bias-correction) $\hat z_0$
and the [acceleration](#def-bca-acceleration) $\hat a$,
for $q \in \cb{\siglevel/2, 1 - \siglevel/2}$, let

$$\adjlevel_q \eqdef \normcdf\paren{\hat{z}_0 + \frac{\hat{z}_0 + z_q}{1 - \hat{a}(\hat{z}_0 + z_q)}}.$$

The **bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) bootstrap confidence interval**
runs from the $\adjlevel_{\adjlevel/2}$ quantile
to the $\adjlevel_{1 - \adjlevel/2}$ quantile
of the bootstrap replicates
[@efron1993introduction, Chapter 14].
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#rem-bca-interval-correction}
#### What the BCa interval corrects

When $\hat{z}_0 = 0$ and $\hat{a} = 0$,
$\adjlevel_q = q$ and the BCa interval is the percentile interval
(@def-bootstrap-ci-percentile).
$\hat{z}_0$ measures how far the bootstrap distribution's median
sits from $\hparam$,
and $\hat{a}$ measures its skewness,
so the BCa interval shifts the percentile interval
to correct for both.
:::
